Potentially worth noting/discussing that Integritee Network, who where the most-backed loser in the last round have entered the current round with a cap of 20,000 (down from 100,000).  

(On a side note, I'm not sure it's right to advertise the chain as "inflation: 0%" on the crowdloan.  There's no general inflation, but it seems likely the chain will mint extra KAB to fund proposals, I think?)
yeah good point - there will be inflation, else it could give impression of fixed cap
Thanks all - gonna review and synthesise this discussion and do a summary post, then we can move to the final refinement of the parameters.

## **KUSAMA AUCTIONS ANALYSIS**

Guys, we (EDG DAO Financial Strategist Team) have collated some data regarding the previous **Kusama Auction Winners** i.e. the total KSM they received, no. of contributors, max cap of Crowd-loans, % of total supply allotted for Crowd-loans etc. We have also estimated the approx no of KAB per KSM that crowdloan contributors can get for a range of total KSM collected and so on. 

I believe this data will be useful for the community to get some insights wrt previous auction rounds and also be useful to come up with more newer and interesting suggestions for the Kabocha crowdloan campaign strategy for the Kusama auction. 

We will be adding more data as we go further, but we **would also like to get your views/suggestions, so that we can add more data and draw more interesting and useful insights from the data which can useful to the community. **

**Link:** [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1LDhh6WgZ8NhxUcl8ZFS0jLEItk4rIlVdrNVNv3tuOFA/edit#gid=293266384](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1LDhh6WgZ8NhxUcl8ZFS0jLEItk4rIlVdrNVNv3tuOFA/edit#gid=293266384)

Thanks [@Advait Rane](/edgeware/account/mW9wgCp5XVmg4and5gEdhBiLLR3wxZpTXgExUhfjBLwk1kt).  Your numbers helped me spot the massive errors in mine!

In the main tables of crowdloan numbers, I think it would be useful to highlight which lines are "won" and which are "ongoing".

And cell D69 - KAB for crowdloans.  Should that be 
=4.9*64000000/100 = ~3.2M KAB (not 320,000)?  I think total supply of KAB is 64M rather than 6.4M?

And the histogram of KSM received vs KSM max cap has cumulative numbers, which isn't really what you wanted to show, I think.
Thanks for identifying the errors. Modified the document with the correct details.
Nice work :)

Edit - clearly Christmas eve isn't the time for me to do maths.  

Re-sanity checking my numbers against Advait's, I think it should have been:
20,000KSM winning the crowdloan --> 156KAB per KSM
100,000KSM winning the crowdloan --> 31KAB per KSM
1KSM buys 29,000EDG, and the EDG --> 290KAB (factor of 100 not the 1000 I had)

We're certainly getting in the realms where the risk of getting out of KSM and into EDG might overcome the extra KAB value gained.

Sanity checking the economics:

If I low-ball the amount of KSM to win the auction at 20,000, with a price of $220 per KSM, so $4.4M.  This would share 3.2M KAB, or 0.72KAB per KSM (so per $220 invested).

If the crowdloan reached a 100,000KSM cap, the reward would be about 0.14KAB per KSM.

$220 (1KSM) buys 29,000 EDG which is (I think) worth 29 KAB.

So, that's a strong incentive to buy EDG and hope everyone else contributed KSM.  

I guess this is the (fairly significant) economic issue we're trying to overcome?

thanks for this, useful to have this laid out. 

[@Ramsey](/edgeware/account/k43sLKozrmQq7d7aqpYCzqiUM7DJgMaMrVsrY1uPQvpZLWT)

I would also note that I have about 25 addresses with some (mostly small) amounts of EDG in them, and I suspect I'm far from unusually - especially among validators.  Have you considered a way that you'd track KSM --> EDG account contributions without creating an auditing / admin nightmare for Ramsey (I assume)?

I'm also uncomfortable with the idea of locking 100% of KAB for some - probably a significant proportion - of holders.  In that case, don't we risk having a chain that does little other than build blocks for 48 weeks, since most people have no KAB to pay fees and transact with?

Sorry, I'm slowly catching up after not being as "in" as I should recently.

Currently, the only cryptocurrency I hold is EDG - most of which is bonded to my (and other community members) validators.  I could and likely would sell a bit of if for KSM if I needed to.

But my first thought is "do we need the extra incentive?"  Obviously, I'm late to the discussion here, so I get to see how the recent crowdloans are going which others didn't when they posted.  But some of the recent slots are going for far less than 100,000 KSM now.

We're setting aside 4.9% of KAB for crowdloans - have I missed whether some of this is reserved for the second slot?  Or is there another way that this fund itself - possibly just the self-interest incentive for KAB holders to maintain the parachain slot?

I'd be inclined to keep things simple and try it first to see what happens before increasing the incentive.  And maybe as a fixed total reward pro-rata to the contributors.  Say set 3% or 4.9% of KAB aside for the first parachain slot crowdloaners.  

If we win a slot with 20,000KSM, the contributors get a bigger proportion than if 100,000KSM is contributed.  I think this incentivises people to get in early - if they are in, and a slot if won before the crowdloan pot gets big, they "win" more.

Try that for 5 weeks of auctions (say) and then mix things up if it's apparent that it's not going to be enough.  ~~I THINK we'll win a slot pretty easily.~~ [EDIT: not so sure after a sanity check - see later post.]

Here is an idea about creating a Crowdloan game that could create some interesting competition, and attract other communities in Kusama ecosystem into Kabocha. 

I have written it in present and past tense, but this is just an idea that is intended to inspire interesting thoughts from other people, and if there is interest we can go ahead with something like the below:

# **Idea for crowdloan game** 

Holders of other tokens have the opportunity to participate in the “Kabocha Crowdloan Game”. 

We’ve taken snapshots of RMRK, KSM and MOVR balances and have assigned buckets of KAB. 

Holders of KSM, RMRK and MOVR will be able to “Activate” their balance in KAB by contributing 10% of the value of KSM that is proportional to the value of each RMRK, MOVR and KSM they hold on balance (stay with me it will be clearer below.) 

## Buckets 

**KSM** (5%) 3.245m KAB 
**RMRK** (2.5%) 1.6225m KAB 
**MOVR** (2.5%) 1.6225m KAB 

**It's a race to reach the cap! **
Because there is a KSM cap and not everyone will activate their balance, you have a chance to attain a very decent stake of KAB. 

## Example 
For example, if you own: 

100KSM ($30000), 
100MOVR ($18500) and 
1000 RMRK ($39000) 

as of ~1st January 2022, then you will need to provide 10% of your balance in dollar value order to activate each balance. 

## Calculation 
- Contributing 10KSM ($3000) will unlock your 100KSM in KAB. (10KSM /100KSM = 10%, therefore the entire 100KSM is activated.) 
- It will unlock 100% of your MOVR ($3000 / $185*100 = >10%) 
- And it will unlock 76.9% of your RMRK ($3000 / $39 * 1000 = 76.9%, which is 769 active RMRK) 


It is unknown how much KAB you will exactly receive until after the auction win, but you may get an awesome amount from each KSM, MOVR and RMRK pot as well as from the general reward pot. (edited)

## Dream Scenario 
- **100k KSM cap achieved**
- **only 2 participants** 


In theory, if the KSM cap is 100,000 KSM, and there were only 2 participants, you and Alice the whale.

**KSM** (5%) 3.245m KAB

Because there is a KSM cap and not everyone will activate their balance, you have a chance to attain a very decent stake of KAB. 

## Example 
For example, if you own:

as of ~1st January 2022, then you will need to provide 10% of your balance in dollar value order to activate each balance. 

## Calculation

- It will unlock 100% of your MOVR ($3000 / $185*100 = >10%) 
- And it will unlock 76.9% of your RMRK ($3000 / $39 * 1000 = 76.9%, which is 769 active RMRK) 


It is unknown how much KAB you will exactly receive until after the auction win, but you may get an awesome amount from each KSM, MOVR and RMRK pot as well as from the general reward pot. (edited)

## Dream Scenario 
- **100k KSM cap achieved**
- **only 2 participants** 


In theory, if the KSM cap is 100,000 KSM, and there were only 2 participants, you and Alice the whale. Alice who only owns KSM, contributed 99.99k KSM and you provided the other 10KSM, which met the 100k KSM cap. You gain an outlandish amount because you will scoop the entire bucket of KAB that was assigned to MOVR and RMRK, which adds up to 3.2m KAB, and Alice will receive almost the entire bucket of KAB in the KSM bucket plus the 4.9% rewards. Which is almost 6.5m KAB. Given that there is only around 70m KAB supply, this is a whale amount for both you and Alice. In reality this would not happen at such an extreme, but it will give you an idea of how you can gain an outsized amount of KAB just by participating before the cap is met. 

## Dilution required 
In order to create this game we need to agree to dilute the 100% snapshot by 10%. 

## **Why is this dilution valuable?** 

a) it will attract new community participants from other relevant communities. 
b) it will attract competition amongst whales and get us a strong cap, which makes us a more potent force. 
c) it will allow the EDG snapshot to be left in tact so that people who own EDG can receive KAB sit back and watch the crowdloan games without having to activate their EDG balance in KAB.

I have hesitated a lot before commenting since many people know I would have a strong incentive bias against this idea. Lots of the arguments above make sense, but this is not where I personally see most of the concerns.
I think most of us can agree on:

1. The idea of incentivizing participation of EDG holders to Kabocha in *some* way is probably very desirable.
2. There is another objective, which is to win a parachain slot. That requires contributing locking up KAB.

Unfortunately, conflating two independent objectives into one proposal is not always very appropriate, as it ignores specific dynamics of each incentive structure.
Many people have already pointed out it will create a sell pressure as some holders (like myself), will need to sell EDG to buy KSM. There is an argument according to which the rate is "very reasonable" but this assumes everyone has an amount of KAB ready to crowdloan, and this is not the case. 
So I am willing to be contributing to the success of Kabocha. What is the path to acquire the KSM required? Is it everyone on its own with an exchange and best of luck?
Then, this creates opportunity for timing attacks in the EDG price, and whoever sets the rate (even if we vote this, whoever defines the possible alternatives, and whoever votes last on tangent cases etc. would have additional information on how much will be sold. Designing a mechanism that is fair and secure is too complicated for this objective alone.

Besides, it seems I am isolated on that one, but I think this this a *major* problem to exclude the Binance/Coinbase wallets from the distribution. The possibility from them to distribute their holding to their massive clientbase is a huge opportunity to grow our community. 

It could also be argued that EDG holders being KAB holders already have an incentive to secure a parachain slot overall. 
A Strong coupling the EDG and KSM incentives in KAB does not appear necessary to me with the information we currently have so why making this all complicated now?
We can maybe achieve some similar effect by not preventing the "recycling" of the EDG if used into the crowdloan.
One thing is that we need to prevent people to opportunisticly aquire EDGjust before and dump it just after the snapshot, we can require EDG to be present on the account for some time to be eligible for unlocking (or equivalently, take the min of the balance over one period that starts before and ends after the crowdloan instead of a discrete "snapshot"). But we can chose to relax this for crowdloaners. To do this properly ideally requires a DEX (with perfectly liquid KSM/EDG, etc. etc., something we haven't got), but we can mimic something similar by endonding some kind of signalling into transactions.
A simple - and probably naive, but for the sake of illustration - way to achieve this would be to first choose a public price oracle with an api (e.g. coingecko), or ask a given partner exchange to provide us with data regarding KSM/EDG price for the period. We can define what the oracle would be in advance.
Then, we require that people wanting to crowdloan to send an EDG transaction (of defined insignificant amount a0) to a given EDG account X set up for that purpose moments before exchanging, and to require that their next transaction would be of insignificant amount a1 to the EDG account whose address corresponds to the Kusama account they will crowdloan with. The script that parses balance would need to do something like this:
1. Start at beginning of locking period and monitor all balances above dust threshold. 
2. Look at every block (or once a day, depending on how heavy that script can be) and take the min of the balance m0 till the end of the locking period. This is the standard distribution method.
To this we add the following:
3. For each incoming transactions to contract X of the defined insignificant amount a0. 
    + Record the balance b0 just before the transaction sending a0.
    + Look whether the next transaction of the sender is of amount a1 and if so, lookup the EDG address and translate to a KSM one. 
    + Lookup the KSM chain for crowdloan information and record the crowdloaned amount c0 in KSM committed to KAB.
    + Use the oracle for KSM/EDG at the time of a0 (we can have some tolerance, since the timing of a0 is the the one of the amount exchange, and the oracle is not the effective exchange price everywhere), and adjust m0 by m0=max(b0,m0+c0*rate)

This example works with public data ( we need to agree on a price source) and with the transaction mechanism only. It just requires users willing to benefit to send two EDG transactions of minimal amounts (it could even be simpler if we can send transaction with DATA like the KSM account address directly). It is fully auditable onchain and only pushes complexity to the script (in particular, monitoring to chains).
This is just an example but I think it is better to create optional incentives, since the coupling becomes looser and optional too.

Just one remark on the longer locking proposed above as an alternative. This is in my opinion a better alternative than enforcing some ratio of EDG/KSM ownership, as above, but it has the downside of preventing people to also participate in other aspects like governance etc. We have a low participation, and the point was precisely to promote activity of different actors (though with activity purely defined as crowdloan participation, which it isn't).

Thanks for this. Gonna need to read this all again tomorrow, but on first pass it makes sense. Keeping things as simple and elegant as possible has been our mantra since the start - no unnessary complexity. 

Agree that the longer locking point proposed by [@Mj de leon](/edgeware/account/ia61WNdrxNM1D6h1zJtHUBMCm9JkGug9wVc2XEEA9E6Ysvz) is a good suggestion. 

[@Ramsey](/edgeware/account/k43sLKozrmQq7d7aqpYCzqiUM7DJgMaMrVsrY1uPQvpZLWT) what do you think on this?

Just fyi, I am not fully bought in to any idea. I would like to go with the best one, and i think there are downsides to changing the incentive design, and like [@Thom Ivy](/edgeware/account/jKauGVPCQkteGTDKuuNwhYhMBrj5QuytgybEC4A5cS4Bki5) mentioned we don't need to necessarily "punish" EDG holders in the design. There are also downsides to keeping everything the same, though that doesn't mean our current inefficient approach will not yield a win. In a vacuum I believe this current design loses, but in reality it could be enough. Though we are relying on outsiders to save us, which is not the strongest position we put ourselves in. 

## **Soft incentives**
The compromise may be to create softer incentives like:

1) **NFT**s; 
2) **locking **KAB balances gained through holding EDG for a **longer** time than KSM as [@Mj de leon](/edgeware/account/ia61WNdrxNM1D6h1zJtHUBMCm9JkGug9wVc2XEEA9E6Ysvz) mentioned. 

## **Why now?**
I think the discussion is brought up now to make sure we all agree to move forward with or without optimising the design of the crowdloan incentives, such that the EDG community can get KAB without participating in the crowdloan, which may yield unwanted outcomes.

## **Incentivising passive behaviour**
For me giving KAB for just having EDG at a certain time incentivises passive behaviour, however this may not just incentivise crowdloan contribution, it may de-incentivise locking up KSM. **Why now?**

**Incentivising passive behaviour**
For me giving KAB for just having EDG at a certain time incentivises passive behaviour, however this may not just incentivise crowdloan contribution, it may de-incentivise locking up KSM. The fact **you** don't have KSM to lock shows that the way we designed this does not incentivise the desired behaviour in people, and therefore this discussion is necessary before we enter a crowdloan campaign. 


## **Re: Activating EDG balance approach**
> Many people have already pointed out it will create a sell pressure as some holders (like myself), will need to sell EDG to buy KSM.
I must say its slightly surprising you dont already have KSM prepared for KAB. But also selling your EDG is not the only way to get KSM: You can exchange some DOT or ETH,  both slightly more liquid than EDG! and also you don't have to activate 100% of your balance, you can activate a portion. 

Would you want to dump some of your EDG holding and create selling pressure for your entire holding in order to activate it for KAB? There will be a natural dynamic here, where the whales dont want to dump EDG. 

**Buying pressure**
With a portion of distribution reserved for "Activating EDG", KSM holders may also buy EDG in order to activate their EDG.
Also we haven't looked at KSM holders who would buy EDG in order to activate it (if we take the Activation approach), which will create buying pressure. 

**KAB is earned not given as a perk for holding EDG.**

------------------------------

**The whales in the room**
Also, having one or two big whales in one cryptocurrency also suppresses price as it centralises attack on price. I believe both you and CW own about 20% of EDG, and most of the politics is built around this. In my view, reducing such whale heaviness (or adding many more whales) will only increase the health. If you both want to activate that balance, it means together roughly locking up ~4,000 KSM in order for both of you whales to keep your balances (if we only decide to activate balance approach). If we go this approach, we can guarantee we win a parachain slot. And thus you will both be whales of a parachain.

**Priorities**
> 1. The idea of incentivizing participation of EDG holders to Kabocha in *some* way is probably very desirable.
> 2. There is another objective, which is to win a parachain slot. That requires contributing locking up KAB.
> Unfortunately, conflating two independent objectives into one proposal is not always very appropriate, as it ignores specific dynamics of each incentive structure.

- Number 1) is not really the main objective it's probably number 3 on the list, but it would promote higher "quorum" of turnout, because it's what people care about. 
- The main objective is to win a parachain slot (number 2). 
- Our other main priority (which we have seemed to prioritised over winning) is how to retain the EDG balances across to KAB? This is the conflation that may cause undesirable outcomes because we are giving people two routes to get KAB, where one of the routes have no positive effect on winning an auction, and it may **de-**incentivise locking KSM. 
- What is also a priority over winning, is protecting the price of EDG, which is defensive, when we probably need to be aggressive. 




**Two Snapshots (beginning and end of lease)**
> One thing is that we need to prevent people to opportunistically aquire EDG just before and dump it just after the snapshot...
From what i understand of your explanation take 2 snapshots: Snapshot #1, 14 days after auction win, and  Snapshot #2, 14 days before the end of 48 week period. 
- **Snapshot #1** reserved distribution is created at snapshot #1. 
- **Snapshot #2 **at the end of the lease, the balances are confirmed to be the same or greater, if the same or greater the account realises 100% of the KAB equity. If it is less (e.g. only 50% of their snapshot 1 balance then they only get 50% of their KAB equity realised. 


**Long term design**
The longer term questions we should be asking is how to retain multiple leases? There is something interesting about keeping the whole community engaged in activating their balance, rather than using inflation for rewarding crowdloans. If we do like everyone does and reward people for essentially voting, then we are competing amongst a large pool, which is inflationary. But if we design such that people have to protect their balance (or at least some of it), then we dont have to inflate the distribution every year, and thus keep inflation for more important funding of human endeavours. There is something resonant here to Kabocha values. 

**Using our own treasury**, simply we can mint coins as KAB and vote in our own parachain lease, which because of undefined treasury (which maybe we should have yearly cap) we can do it easier than other communities. 

**Striking a balance**
Instead of either/or, we can have best of both.

There can be a sweet spot of splitting the 90.2% distribution in half and having 45.1% for EDG snapshot, and 45.1% Activate Balance. If very few people activate their balance and we still win an auction, then the pool for Active Balance will be a major incentive for people to receive a reward and become bigger KAB whale.

45.1% - EDG snapshot 1:1 EDG to KAB 
45.1% - Activate EDG - if you vote with KSM with ~6% of your EDG balance then you get equivalent 1:1 EDG to KAB.

Here, we also protect some Binance and Coinbase distribution. My argument here is why are binance balances so important? i believe this has what been keeping Edgeware distracted for so long. Wouldnt it be better to tap into more relevant reservoirs of value, such as taking snapshot of DOT, KSM, MOVR, KAR or RMRK! and giving value to people who are already understanding of KSM and crowdloans. 

We are probably missing many tricks. And why we have to be locked into a very inefficient, not-very-well designed system because we dont want to upset people who speculated on what were always "tentative" plans seems like misplaced judgements. 

We may be lucky, and competitive advantages are inefficient enough for us to simply win an auction with the 4.9% crowdloan. 

But the above is food for thought!

body: I'm supporting the idea to have KAB pool splitted as you proposed ... this seems to be fair enough under current conditions, also 2 snapshots model is very reasonable, snapshot days should be announced in advance so holders have enough time to prepare ( I'm ok with proposed: Snapshot # 1, 14 days after auction win, and Snapshot # 2, 14 days before the end of 48 week period). Regarding ration needed for smaller holders vs bigger holders, well in my opinion terms should be equal to everyone if we are going to stick with this model.

**EDG holder only** = can get their kab with 48 weeks distribution period

**Best case**

The 4.9% slotted for KSM crowndloan incentives will suffice, with no further issue.  **Edit:** If this is thought to be insufficient, the KAB treasury can be reduced to cover more KSM crowdloan participant incentives- but would leave less for public use after launch. 



**Second best case**
The EDG treasury can be tapped for helping users recoup the cost of their 'activated' amount. e.g. Prove you locked KSM equal to your activation cost, and the treasury will reward you in the equivalent value in EDG. Yes, it's a shame to complicate the process, but in this way users are made whole in a sort of decentralized way, but it's an act of the public investing more network share in those willing to make the steps. 

**Third best case:**
If the second best case fails to secure enough KSM, the treasury might be proposed to in order to run an OTC to acquire the remaining KSM estimated. This is highly conditional on finding those buyers, obviously. 

In this way, KAB has three steps it can try independently, trying the next if one fails, and avoiding punishing EDG holders directly who may have joined on the premise of an non-participatory airdrop by targeting our shared public wealth instead.

Our aim with Kabocha has been to keep it simple and fair from the start - to make everything as easy to understand and implement as possible. 

Right now, this discussion is centred around a single debate:

_**In order to acquire the KSM required, should we encourage our community of EDG holders to also contribute KSM to the crowdloan in return for receiving their KAB?**_

That's a simple Yes/No which will be what the soft signal  vote is focused on. 

_**If so, how do we do this in a simple, fair and community led way as possible?**_

The follow on questions to that primary point are:

1. What is the incentive?
2. Is there a multiplier?
3. How does that work in practice w/distribution


So right now, I'm not too worried about distribution questions - practically speaking if we get there, then it will be the simplest and most easy to understand and implement approach. 

So yes - if we keep things simple, we will be using the same 90.2% pool and yes to the 4.9%. for additional rewards, but we are not there yet.
